key_insight: For traumatic brain injury prediction, simpler ML models can deliver nearly the same clinical benefit as more complex models while using far less compute and carbon.
clinical_relevance: In digital health deployment, especially in resource-limited settings, model choice should balance predictive performance with feasibility, cost, and environmental impact.
method: External validation in a level 1 trauma center with 534 adult TBI patients.
Compared 7 ML models: 2 pauci-parameter models and 5 multiparameter models.
Evaluated discrimination, net clinical benefit, inference time, and carbon footprint.
evidence_signal: The best complex model had about 100× longer inference time and 10× higher emissions per prediction, yet net clinical benefit was nearly the same as simpler models.
watch_item: Results came from a single-center external validation cohort, so broader generalizability and real-world implementation performance still need confirmation.
paper_title: Is simple better? Comparing Computational Cost and Carbon Impact of Machine Learning Models for Traumatic Brain Injury Prediction; A Case Study for Sustainable Digital Health Implementation
